task: A library has 1,200 books. It donates 12% of its collection to a school. It then purchases 84 new books. Afterwards it discards 5% of the books it now has. Finally it receives a donation of 90 books. How many books are in the library after these actions?

A bakery starts the week baking 120 loaves. Each subsequent day it bakes 25 more loaves than the previous day. After five days it has baked a total of loaves. It then donates 20% of the loaves and packs the remaining loaves into baskets that hold six loaves each. How many loaves are left unpacked?

A construction site begins with 4,800 bricks. Each day the crew lays 15% of the bricks they have at the start of that day. After two days they receive a delivery of 932 bricks. Then they lay 20% of the bricks they now have. How many bricks remain?

A farmer harvests apples over three weeks. In the first week he picks 800 apples, in the second week 20% more than the first, and in the third week 20% more than the second. He packs the apples into crates that hold 48 apples each. He sells a quarter of the crates and gives away 10 crates to a school. How many apples are left unpacked?

A car rental agency starts a month with 150 cars available. Each month 8% of the available cars are sent for maintenance and are unavailable the next month, while the agency adds 12 new cars each month. After four months, how many cars are available for rent?

A theater sells tickets for three nights. Night 1: 320 tickets at $15 each. Night 2: price increased by 10% and 280 tickets sold. Night 3: price reduced by $2 from night 2’s price and 300 tickets sold. The theater then donates 20% of the total revenue from the three nights. How many dollars are donated?

A delivery truck starts with 600 liters of diesel and uses fuel at 8 liters per 100 km. It drives 150 km north, refuels 120 liters, drives 200 km east, then after unloading cargo its fuel consumption increases to 10 liters per 100 km for the rest of the trip. It then drives 180 km south to its destination. How many liters of diesel remain?

A chemist needs 200 liters of a solution that is 40% acid. She first adds 80 liters of a 30% acid solution, then adds some liters of a 70% acid solution, and finally adds enough water (0% acid) to reach the desired 200 liters. How many liters of water does she add?

A conference hall has 250 seats arranged in rows of 10 seats each. There are 5 keynote speakers, each accompanied by 2 assistants. The remaining seats are occupied by attendees. How many rows are fully or partially occupied by attendees?

A factory runs three machines that produce widgets. Machine X makes 100 widgets per hour, Machine Y makes 150% of X’s hourly output, and Machine Z makes twice as many per hour as Machine Y. Machine X runs for 4 hours, Machine Y for 3 hours, and Machine Z for 2 hours. After production, 18% of the total widgets are defective and are discarded. How many non‑defective widgets remain?

A library received 500 new books. It cataloged 10% of them on Monday, then shelved 90 books on Tuesday. On Wednesday it donated 15% of the remaining uncataloged books to another branch. How many books are left uncataloged after Wednesday?

A factory produces widgets. In the first shift it makes 120 widgets. In the second shift it works at 80% of the first shift's output. In the third shift it produces 30 more widgets than the second shift. After the three shifts, the factory packages the widgets into boxes of 24 each, with any leftover widgets stored separately. How many widgets remain unpacked after packaging?

A chef plans to make a large batch of soup. The recipe calls for 1 cup of carrots per 3 liters of broth. The chef has 18 liters of broth ready. He first adds the required carrots, then decides to increase the carrot amount by 25% and adds more broth to keep the original ratio. After these adjustments, he ends up with 30 liters of broth. How many cups of carrots are in the final soup?

An investor deposits $12,000 into an account that earns 5% interest compounded annually. After one year, she withdraws $500 for expenses. She then adds an additional deposit of $1,200 at the beginning of the second year. The account continues to earn the same annual interest, and at the end of the second year she withdraws $800. How much money is in the account after the second withdrawal?

A building project requires 9,600 kilograms of steel beams. The steel is delivered in bundles, each weighing 240 kilograms. After the first day, 15% of the bundles are set aside for later use, and the remaining bundles are cut into pieces each weighing 30 kilograms. How many 30‑kilogram pieces are produced from the bundles used on the first day?

A music festival sells three types of tickets: standard for $45, premium for $75, and VIP for $120. On the first day, 160 tickets are sold, with twice as many standard tickets as premium tickets, and the remaining are VIP tickets. On the second day, ticket sales increase by 25% overall, and the ratio of premium to standard tickets sold that day is 3:5, with no VIP tickets sold. How many VIP tickets were sold in total over the two days?

A painter needs to mix two colors of paint to obtain a final batch of 84 liters with a ratio of 7 parts blue to 5 parts yellow. He first mixes 24 liters following the correct ratio, then decides to add more yellow paint to achieve a final ratio of 2 parts blue to 3 parts yellow while keeping the amount of blue paint unchanged. How many liters of yellow paint does he add in the second step?

A warehouse stores boxes each weighing 20 kg. A pallet can hold at most 15 boxes due to size constraints, and the weight limit of 400 kg is not exceeded. Initially, the manager loads each pallet with the maximum number of boxes allowed by the size constraint. After loading, he decides to consolidate the boxes so that each pallet carries the same number of boxes and the total number of pallets used is reduced by 2. How many boxes are on each pallet after the consolidation?

A school district operates buses that travel at 48 km/h. On Monday, Bus A covers a route of 288 km. On Tuesday, Bus B starts from the same depot, travels the same route but at a speed that is 20% faster, and after completing the route, it immediately returns to the depot at the original speed of 48 km/h. How many total hours does Bus B spend on the round trip?

A farmer has 1,200 acres of land. He plans to plant corn on 40% of the acres and wheat on the rest. Each acre of corn requires 3 bags of fertilizer and 2 irrigation cycles, while each acre of wheat requires 2 bags of fertilizer and 3 irrigation cycles. The farmer has 2,700 bags of fertilizer and enough water for 1,800 irrigation cycles. After planting, he decides to increase the corn area by 10% of the original total acreage and decrease the wheat area accordingly, keeping the total acreage the same. How many bags of fertilizer will be used after this adjustment?

A factory operates 5 machines that each produce 120 gadgets per day. After production, 20% of the gadgets are defective and removed. On Monday the factory sells 150 gadgets, and on Tuesday it sells two‑thirds of the remaining gadgets. How many gadgets are left at the end of Tuesday?

A library starts with 1,000 books. Each month it adds 20% more books for three consecutive months. After the three months, it discards 150 books due to damage. Then it lends out 250 books each month for the next two months. How many books remain after these two months?

A bakery uses 4 ovens, each baking 30 loaves per day. After baking, it sells 40% of the loaves in the morning, donates 15 loaves in the afternoon, then bakes an additional 21 loaves in the evening. Finally it sells half of the loaves that are left after the evening bake. How many loaves are left at the end of the day?

A farmer begins the week with 100 bags of cement. Each bag weighs 25 kg. He uses 30% of the bags for the foundation on Monday. On Tuesday he receives 10% more bags than he received on Monday and then uses 15% of the total bags (including Monday's remaining) for the walls. On Wednesday he ships the remaining bags to another site. How many bags are shipped on Wednesday?

A car‑rental agency has a fleet of 200 cars. Each month it retires 12% of the fleet and immediately replaces each retired car with a new one. After the replacement, 15% of the cars are sent for maintenance, reducing the number of available cars. The agency then rents out 30 cars per week for four weeks. How many cars are still available after the four weeks?

A farmer collects 432 eggs and packs them into cartons that hold 12 eggs each. He sells two‑thirds of the full cartons on Saturday. The remaining cartons are stored, but each night 8 eggs break. After three nights he repacks the remaining eggs into cartons of 15 eggs each and sells half of these new cartons. How many eggs are left unsold after this?

An aquarium has three tanks with capacities of 50 L, 70 L, and 90 L. Water costs $2 per litre. After filling each tank completely, decorative stones are placed that occupy 10% of each tank’s volume, displacing water. Then each tank’s filter consumes 5 L of water per day for six days. How many litres of water remain in the tanks after six days?

A theater originally has 12 rows of 20 seats each. For a special performance it removes 2 seats from each of the first 5 rows and adds 10 seats to each of the last 3 rows. Afterwards, 15% of the total seats are booked for the show, and then 8 seats become unavailable due to maintenance. How many seats are still available for sale?

A shipping company receives 180 packages in the morning. It immediately sends out 25% of them as priority shipments. The rest are stored in a warehouse. In the afternoon it receives an additional batch of packages (size unknown). After the afternoon batch arrives, the company ships out 40% of all packages currently in the warehouse. At the end of the day 84 packages remain in the warehouse. How many packages were in the afternoon batch?

A bakery bakes 8 trays of cupcakes on Monday, 25 cupcakes per tray. It sells 40% of the cupcakes that day. On Tuesday it bakes 5 trays of 30 cupcakes each and then gives away 10% of the total cupcakes produced so far to a charity. On Wednesday it sells twice the number of cupcakes it gave away on Tuesday. After Wednesday it has 140 cupcakes left. How many cupcakes were given away on Tuesday?

A warehouse has 480 boxes. First, 10% of the boxes are damaged and removed. Then 30 boxes are shipped out. The remaining boxes are packed into crates that hold 24 boxes each, leaving one crate partially filled. How many boxes are in the partially filled crate?

A school has 350 students. 20% attend the music club. Half of those music club members also join the sports team. The sports team has 60 members in total, including those who are also in the music club. How many students are on the sports team but not in the music club?

A bakery produces 720 loaves each week. On Monday it sells 15% of the weekly production. On Tuesday it bakes an extra 78 loaves. That same Tuesday it sells 30% of the loaves then on hand. At the end of Tuesday the unsold loaves are packed into boxes of 12, leaving a few loaves that do not fill a box. How many loaves are left over?

A farmer harvests 1,250 apples. He sells one‑fifth of them at the market. He then gives away 140 apples to a charity. The remaining apples are stored in crates that hold 80 apples each, filling 10 crates completely and placing the rest in one partially filled crate. How many apples are in the partially filled crate?

A construction company needs 4,000 bricks for a project. They receive a shipment that is 25% larger than needed. They use one‑quarter of the received bricks for the foundation. After that, they allocate 250 bricks for the chimney. The remaining bricks are packed into pallets that hold 139 bricks each, leaving five pallets partially filled. How many bricks are on each of those partially filled pallets?

A library has 9,600 books. Fifteen percent are reference books and are not lent out. Of the remaining books, 40% are checked out each month. After the first month the library purchases 804 new books, 500 of which are reference books. In the second month, they again check out 40% of the currently non‑reference books. How many non‑reference books are still on the shelves after the second month?

A travel agency plans a tour for 180 participants. Thirty percent are adults and the rest are children. Each adult pays $250 and each child pays $150. Exactly 60 adults register early, qualifying the group for a 10% early‑bird discount on the total revenue. After applying the discount, the agency adds a fixed service fee of $2,000. What is the final amount collected?

A factory produces 3,200 gadgets in a week. Twenty‑five percent are model X and the rest are model Y. Model X gadgets sell for $45 each, model Y for $30 each. The factory has a weekly overhead of $12,000 and a variable production cost of $10 per gadget. After selling all gadgets, what is the net profit?

A gardener plants 1,200 seedlings: 40% tomatoes, 35% peppers, and the remainder lettuce. After two weeks, half of the tomato seedlings survive, 80% of the pepper seedlings survive, and 90% of the lettuce survive. The gardener sells surviving lettuce at $2 each, peppers at $3 each, and tomatoes at $4 each. How much total revenue does the gardener earn?

An event hall seats 1,500 guests. For a conference, 60% of the seats are allocated to attendees, 25% to speakers, and the rest to staff. Each attendee pays $80; speakers attend for free; each staff member receives a $30 stipend paid by the organizers. After the conference the organizers receive a sponsorship of $20,000. What is the net amount the organizers spend (negative profit) after accounting for all revenues and expenses?

A factory produces 480 gadgets per day. On Monday it operates at 80% capacity, on Tuesday it runs at full capacity but 30 gadgets are defective and scrapped, on Wednesday it increases production by adding 25% of Monday's output to its normal output, and on Thursday it produces 15% fewer than its full‑capacity output. How many non‑defective gadgets are produced in total over the four days?

A bookstore has 1,200 books. It sells 12% of its inventory on Saturday, receives a new shipment of 312 books on Sunday, then sells twice the number sold on Saturday on Monday, and finally donates 5% of the remaining stock to a library on Tuesday. How many books are left after Tuesday?

A delivery company transports parcels. In the morning it loads 750 parcels onto trucks and delivers 40% of them before lunch. After lunch it receives an additional 180 parcels and loads them. By the end of the day it delivers twice the number delivered in the morning and returns 15 parcels to the depot for re‑routing. How many parcels are still in the trucks at the end of the day?

A farmer has 1,600 eggs. He sells 20% to a local market on Monday, 15% of the remaining on Tuesday, and on Wednesday he packs the rest into cartons of 12 eggs each, with 8 leftover eggs that he gives away. How many full cartons does he ship on Wednesday?

A construction crew has 48 wooden planks, each 2 meters long. They cut 1/4 of the planks into pieces that are 25 cm long each, using the entire length of those planks. The remaining planks are each cut into two equal pieces. How many plank pieces (of any length) do they have after all cuts?

A zoo has 240 reptiles. In January, they transfer 20% of them to another zoo. In February, they acquire 28 new reptiles. In March, they move 30% of the remaining reptiles to a different exhibit within the same zoo, and then they release 12 reptiles to the wild. How many reptiles are still in the zoo after March?

A theater has 1,200 seats. For the opening night, 55% of seats are sold. The next day, they sell an additional 180 tickets. On the third day, they hold a special promotion that sells double the number of tickets sold on the second day, but only for the remaining unsold seats. After the promotion, they close the box office and report that 10% of the seats that were ever sold remain unoccupied due to no‑shows. How many seats are occupied on the third day?

A bakery produces loaves of bread. On Monday it bakes 350 loaves and sells 60% of them by the end of the day. On Tuesday it bakes 150 more loaves and sells 80% of the total loaves (including any leftover from Monday). On Wednesday it donates 20 loaves to a shelter and then packages the remaining loaves into bags of 5 loaves each for delivery. How many bags does the bakery prepare on Wednesday?

A car rental company has a fleet of 500 cars. At the start of the month, 10% are under maintenance. Of the remaining cars, 30% are rented out for the first week. During the second week, the company purchases 25 new cars and retires none. By the end of the second week, they have rented out an additional 15% of the cars that were available at the start of that week. At the end of the month, 4% of the total fleet is scheduled for a future upgrade and will be taken out of service. How many cars are still available for rental at month’s end?

A science lab has 720 test tubes. On Monday, they fill 2/3 of them with samples. On Tuesday, they use half of the filled tubes for experiments, and the remaining filled tubes are sealed. On Wednesday, they acquire 96 new empty test tubes and decide to fill 25% of all currently empty tubes (including the newly acquired ones). After that, they discard any sealed tubes that are older than 5 days, which amount to 40 tubes. How many filled test tubes are in the lab at the end of Wednesday?

A store starts with 500 items. On Monday it sells 12% of its stock. On Tuesday it receives a shipment of 150 items. On Wednesday it sells twice the number sold on Monday. On Thursday it sells 20% of the items remaining after Wednesday. How many items are left after Thursday?

A bakery bakes 240 loaves each day. On Monday it sells 30% of the day's production. On Tuesday it bakes 10% more loaves than Monday's production and sells 50 loaves. On Wednesday it bakes half as many loaves as the total number sold on Monday and Tuesday combined, and sells all of them. How many loaves were baked on Wednesday?

A construction crew starts a project with 6,000 bricks. On Monday they build 5 walls, each requiring 480 bricks. After Monday they receive a delivery of 400 bricks. On Tuesday they increase the number of walls they build by 20% compared to Monday. After Tuesday they have exactly 1,120 bricks left. How many bricks did they use on Tuesday?

A factory produces 2,500 widgets in the first week. Fifteen percent are defective and discarded. In the second week production rises by 10% and twelve percent of those are defective. In the third week production falls by 20% relative to the second week and five percent are defective. How many non‑defective widgets are produced in total over the three weeks?

An agency books 180 seats on a bus at $100 each. On day 1, 40% of the passengers cancel and are refunded $75 each. On day 2, the agency sells additional seats equal to 25% of the remaining bookings at $80 each. On day 3, 30% of the current passengers receive a $10 discount on their tickets. What total revenue (in dollars) is earned after refunds and discounts?

A rectangular field is 120 m long and 80 m wide. The farmer plants corn on 60% of the area, wheat on 30%, and leaves the rest fallow. Corn needs 3 kg fertilizer per 100 m², wheat needs 2 kg per 100 m². Fertilizer is bought in 25‑kg bags. How many whole bags must be purchased to fertilize the planted area?

An airline flight seats 300 passengers. The flight is 80% full, with business class comprising 25% of the sold seats. Economy tickets cost $200, business tickets $500. Additionally, 10% of economy passengers receive a $20 discount. What is the total revenue from this flight?

A car‑rental company has a fleet of 200 cars: 40% compact, 35% midsize, the rest SUVs. Compact cars rent for $30 per day and are rented 5 days each; midsize rent for $45 per day and are rented 4 days each; SUVs rent for $60 per day and are rented 6 days each. What is the total rental income for one week?

A school library holds 3,600 books: 45% fiction, 35% non‑fiction, the rest reference. It donates 20% of its fiction books and 10% of its non‑fiction books. Afterwards it purchases new reference books equal to half the total number donated. How many books does the library have now?

A catering company must serve 250 guests. Each guest receives a main dish and a dessert. Main dishes: chicken ($8 each), beef ($10 each), vegetarian ($7 each). The plan is to serve chicken to twice as many guests as beef, and vegetarian to the remaining guests, which results in 70 vegetarian meals. Desserts: 60% of guests get a cake slice ($3 each) and the rest get a fruit platter ($4 each). What is the total cost of all meals?

A horticulture center has 3,600 potted plants. Each tray holds 15 plants. On Monday they sell 10% of the trays. On Tuesday they donate 120 plants to a school, taking the plants from full trays only. On Wednesday they receive a shipment of 2,250 plants and place them onto new trays that hold 25 plants each. Finally, they move 3% of the remaining plants to the special collection, taking them from full 15‑plant trays. How many full trays are there at the end of Wednesday?

A library holds 12,000 books. Shelves accommodate 40 books each. On the first day, 5% of the shelves are removed for renovation. The next day 1,200 books are lent out. Then the library receives a donation of 4,800 books, placing them on new shelves that hold 48 books each. Afterwards, a new regulation reduces the usable shelf space by 4%, and the library moves the equivalent number of books to an off‑site collection, taking them from the original 40‑book shelves only. How many shelves remain in the library after these actions?

A bakery makes 9,600 loaves of bread each week. Each crate holds 24 loaves. On Monday they pack 15% of the loaves into crates for wholesale. On Tuesday they sell 1,080 loaves directly to customers. On Wednesday they receive an order for 2,160 loaves, which they pack into new crates that hold 30 loaves each. On Thursday they donate 5% of the loaves that are still unpacked to a food bank. How many crates are in storage at the end of Thursday?

A delivery company operates 12 trucks. Each truck can travel 400 miles on a full tank of 10 gallons of diesel (40 mpg). At the start of the week each tank is full. On Monday the fleet collectively travels 1,600 miles. On Tuesday each truck refuels 5 gallons. On Wednesday a regulation reduces fuel efficiency by 10% (new efficiency 36 mpg). On Thursday the fleet together travels 2,160 miles. How many gallons of diesel remain in all trucks combined at the end of Thursday?

A construction site initially has 14 pallets of bricks, each pallet containing 500 bricks. On the first day they use 20% of the bricks for foundations. The next day they receive a delivery of 1,800 bricks, storing them in new pallets that hold 500 bricks each. On the third day they allocate 15% of the remaining bricks to build a wall, taking the bricks from the inventory without regard to pallet fullness. Finally, they discover that 4 pallets are each half‑full. How many bricks are in those half‑full pallets combined?

A community garden has 84 vegetable beds, each initially containing 30 tomato plants. On Monday they harvest 20% of the plants. On Tuesday they transplant 168 new seedlings, placing them equally among the beds. On Wednesday they apply a fertilizer that increases the number of plants in each bed by 25%, rounding down to the nearest whole plant per bed. On Thursday they remove 5% of the total plants for a local market. How many tomato plants remain in the garden at the end of Thursday?

A theater contains 1,250 seats. On Monday, 40% of the seats are sold at full price. On Tuesday, the theater offers a 25% discount and sells half as many tickets as were sold on Monday. On Wednesday, 10% of the tickets sold on Tuesday are refunded. On Thursday, a group reservation occupies 8% of the remaining unsold seats. How many seats are still unsold at the end of Thursday?

A rectangular swimming pool holds 96,000 liters when full. Each day, 1.5% of the water evaporates. On the second day the manager adds 240 liters of fresh water. On the third day a chemical is added that requires 0.25% of the current volume of water. After these three days the pool is drained to a maintenance level that is exactly 80% of its original full capacity. How many liters of water are removed during the draining?

A factory produces 14,400 gadgets each week. Each gadget requires 3 components. On Monday, 20% of the finished gadgets are found to have a minor defect and are set aside for rework. On Tuesday the rework team fixes 80% of the set‑aside gadgets, discarding the rest. On Wednesday the factory receives a shipment of 1,308 additional components, which are used to assemble extra gadgets (each gadget needs 3 components). On Thursday, 5% of all good (non‑defective) gadgets are shipped out. How many gadgets remain in inventory at the end of Thursday?

A school district operates 9 buses, each with a capacity of 56 students. On Monday each bus transports 78% of its capacity to school. On Tuesday each bus makes a second trip, picking up the remaining students, but 5% of those students are absent and stay home. On Wednesday the district adds 3 new buses, each with a capacity of 48 students, and they run the same two‑trip schedule as Monday and Tuesday (full capacity on first trip, second trip picks up the remaining students with the same 5% absentee rate). On Thursday each bus uses 3 gallons of fuel per trip. After all trips for Thursday, the district refuels each bus back to a full 20‑gallon tank. How many gallons of fuel are purchased in total for the refueling?
